🇲🇽💰 <u>Mexican workers' retirement funds gain 700 billion pesos in 2026</u>

Despite a volatile year in global markets, Mexico's retirement savings system (SAR) racked up gains of 700,384 million pesos between January and October, according to Consar. October alone added 209,427 million pesos. The money belongs to workers' Afore accounts, and Consar head Julio César Cervantes confirmed at the Amafore 2026 meeting that the year's gains have already passed 700 billion.

🇲🇽⛏️ <u>Mexico is the world's #1 silver producer. Should silver back the peso?</u>

Mexico supplies about 24% of the world's silver, more than 200 million ounces a year, ahead of China and Peru. It is also second in fluorite, fifth in lead and sixth in zinc, with copper, lithium clay and traces of uranium and thorium mapped by the Mexican Geological Service. In Contralínea, Pablo Moctezuma Barragán argues that Banxico could put part of its reserves of more than $250 billion into physical silver to back the currency and "reduce dependence on the US dollar."

🇲🇽🚌 <u>Veracruz modernizes public transit with no private operators and no debt</u>

Veracruz is rebuilding its bus systems with a public trust: fare revenue covers fuel, wages and maintenance, and the rest goes back into buying new units. "The model involves no private companies and no financing costs," Governor Rocío Nahle said, which keeps fares affordable without putting the state in debt. Four systems already run in Veracruz-Boca del Río, Coatzacoalcos-Minatitlán, Cosamaloapan and Poza Rica. The fifth, Atenas, launches November 23 in Xalapa with 60 buses to serve 900,000 riders a month.

🇲🇽❤️ <u>Sheinbaum to AMLO on his 73rd birthday: "our affection, recognition, admiration, always"</u>

Andrés Manuel López Obrador turned 73 on November 13 at his ranch in Palenque, Chiapas, far from public life since leaving office in 2024. From the National Palace, President Sheinbaum sent the country's greeting: "From here, our affection, recognition, admiration, always." Interior Secretary Rosa Icela Rodríguez, Attorney General Ernestina Godoy, Welfare Secretary Leticia Ramírez, Morena leader Ariadna Montiel and Mexico City Mayor Clara Brugada joined in.

🚨🇲🇽 <u>A US air-traffic meltdown strands 18,000 passengers in Mexico</u>

Washington shut down its entire airspace for four and a half hours on November 13, and Mexico paid for it. Mexico's civil aviation agency (AFAC) counted 193 flights and 18,002 passengers hit at Mexican airports. At Mexico City's AICM alone, 44 flights were cancelled and 29 delayed, affecting 10,293 travelers. The FAA's explanation: a contractor failure and "a faulty router." Now the Trump administration wants Congress to pay for new systems.

text: ‍FOX 5 DC: ICE plans to deport UMD student, mother to Mexico as court order bars El Salvador deportation: Attorney November 13, 2026 | 🟡 📰 ICE plans to deport a Salvadoran UMD freshman and her mother to Mexico, because a 2021 court order bars sending them to El Salvador. Neither has a criminal record. 🔍 Mexico is the destination under a March 2025 third-country removal policy. The only voices on Mexico are the family's attorney, who says Mexico "regularly buses Salvadorans" home, and DHS. No Mexican official is asked whether Mexico agreed to take them. • "ICE wants to send them to a country that will." • "a country that is not theirs"

text: ‍NY POST: LA gangster 'Fat Boy' helped Olympic snowboarder turned drug kingpin run billion-dollar trafficking ring: feds November 13, 2026 | 🟡 📰 NY Post covers a member of South LA's 38th Street gang who is accused of feeding law-enforcement intel to ex-Olympian Ryan Wedding's cocaine network. The lede is "Mexican cartels." 🔍 Mexico's role is mostly in passive voice. Wedding "was arrested in Mexico City," and no arresting agency is named. Lower down, the story mentions Mexican police killing a co-defendant and Mexico arresting a judge over a $2M bribe. • "worked with Mexican cartels and leaked law-enforcement intelligence" • "arrested in Mexico City in January and flown back to the US"

text: ‍KJZZ: Mexico receives 11 responses from U.S. prosecutors over ICE deaths November 13, 2026 | 🟢 📰 KJZZ reports the count from Mexico's side: 18 Mexican nationals have died in ICE custody or during enforcement operations since January 2025. Mexico's foreign ministry has sent 22 letters to US prosecutors and received 11 replies. 🇲🇽 One case is Lorenzo Salgado Araujo, 52, shot dead by an ICE officer during a traffic stop in Houston. Two more Mexicans have died in ICE custody in Arizona. • "eight to state attorneys general and 14 to county prosecutors"

‍AP/ABC: Brother of Mexican cartel leader sentenced to 22 years for drug trafficking plot November 13, 2026 | 🟢 📰 AP covers the 22-year US sentence for Antonio Oseguera, El Mencho's brother, and credits Mexico: the Mexican government handed him over last year, and the Mexican army killed El Mencho in February. 🔍 The case is still filed under a "broader Trump administration effort." His lawyers note he had already spent years in a Mexican prison for essentially the same conduct. • "the Mexican government handed him over to U.S. authorities" • "there may be no nonviolent drug cartels in Mexico"

‍AP/MPR: U.S. and Mexico risk losing a major health victory: What to know November 14, 2026 | 🟢 📰 AP's measles explainer is straight on the cause. US childhood vaccination fell to about 92%, RFK Jr. downsized the childhood schedule, and Trump called the MMR vaccine possibly "quite lethal." 🇲🇽 It also traces Mexico's outbreak to its source: an unvaccinated Mennonite child from Chihuahua who traveled to Gaines County, Texas, and came back infected. Mexico now has more than 20,500 cases and 50 deaths, most of them children under 5. • "The decision represents us moving backward" • "The measles elimination designation is not what protects Americans"
